chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Talhah ibn Zayd, from Ja'far, from his father, upon them be peace, who said:

I read in the book of Ali (peace be upon him): 'If a man marries a woman and commits zina (fornication/adultery) with her before consummating the marriage (entering into her), she is not permissible to him because he is a zani (one who commits zina), and they are separated, and he gives her half of the dowry (sadaq).'

key_terms.يَدْخُلَ بِهَا: To enter into her (consummate the marriage)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on marriage separation and dowry if zina occurs before consummation?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* attributes a specific fiqh ruling to Imam Ali (AS) regarding the dissolution of marriage due to zina prior to consummation, distinguishing it from standard khula or faskh scenarios. It establishes that the husband may separate from the wife while she retains half the dowry (sadaq), reflecting the principle that the right to consummation was not fully realized despite the contract's validity. This highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the precise timing of zina relative to dakhil (consummation) in determining financial liabilities.
